citation: Hanselman, P., & Borman, G. D. (2013). The impacts of Success for All on reading achievement in grades 3-5: Does intervening during the later elementary grades produce the same benefits as intervening early? Educational Evaluation and Policy Analysis, 35(2), 237-251. https://doi.org/10.3102/0162373712466940
design: Cluster RCT; school-level random assignment; 35 schools (17 SFA / 18 control); subject = reading/literacy (Success for All 'Reading Wings' later-elementary component vs business-as-usual); grades 3-5. Two cross-sectional cohorts: primary cohort (3rd grade in 2002-03, followed 3 years to grade 5) and secondary cohort (4th grade in 2002-03, followed 2 years to grade 5). Outcome = Gates-MacGinitie Reading Test (GMRT) 4th ed., levels 3-5, form S.
problems: ICC / design-effect intra-class correlation is not reported anywhere in the paper, so icc is left null (NOT guessed); however cluster_adjusted=true because the impact estimates come from a 2-level HLM that already accounts for school-level clustering, and the reported SEs already reflect the cluster design. Impact estimates ARE already in standardized-effect-size units: the posttest outcome was standardized to M=0, SD=1 within each cohort and year (p.240), so the SFA HLM coefficient (gamma_02) equals d and its SE is on the SD=1 scale. g = J*d using the t-test df reported in Table 4; g_se = J*SE. End-of-treatment waves (the headline contrasts for the meta-analysis) are grade 5 for BOTH cohorts: Cohort 1 Year 3 (g=0.019) and Cohort 2 Year 2 (g=-0.078); these are flagged outcome_role=primary. Intermediate waves (grades 3,4) are included as additional timepoints (outcome_role=secondary) for traceability. Year 3 (Cohort 1) results carry the authors' own caution about differential student attrition (635 vs 434; chi2 p<.01) -- still extracted but noted. GMRT is a standardized, independent, nationally-normed test, so all contrasts are standardized_independent.
